tn_bee_rock.blurb: Bee Rock is a small sandstone cliff on the Cumberland Plateau at Monterey, a few minutes off the interstate, and it is one of the older climbing spots on the plateau. This part of the cliff holds a dozen routes: mostly bolted sport lines, a few trad climbs and a single top-rope. Grades start around 5.6 and run past 5.13, with the bulk in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, so a mixed group can find something. The climbing is technical face work rather than big overhanging moves. Every route sits below the overlook, which makes it a handy after-work or half-day stop.
tn_bee_rock.parking_note: Leave the car in the overlook lot above the cliff.
tn_bee_rock.approach: Scramble down a steep third-class gully located behind the viewpoint, then follow the trail along the foot of the cliff to reach the routes, all of which lie beneath the viewpoint.
